Hmm, I'm confusing myself. So the slots are 4x4 cells! Slot positions (top-left): (18,11),(18,17),(18,23),(18,29),(18,35) — spacing 6 (4-cell slot + 2 gap). And the vertical slots: (24,41),(28,41),(32,41),(36,41),(40,41)? blob4 is at rows 24-27, columns 41-44 → slot (24,41). blob5 is at rows 36-39, columns 41-44 → slot (36,41). Spacing 4?? 24→36 is 12 = 3 slots of 4? Hmm, vertical slots: 24,28,32,36,40 (spacing 4, no gap). But the horizontal spacing is 6. Oh well.
Now T5: I clicked (19,12). The target ring at slot (18,11) spans rows 18-21, columns 11-14 (hollow: (18,12),(18,13),(19,11),(19,14),(20,11),(20,14),(21,12),(21,13)). OK, no asymmetry there.
So the T5 vs T10 asymmetry remains: leftward crossing jump = catastrophe? Or...
Ah, wait. I just thought of something. What if the catastrophe rule is: a jump crosses a blob AND the crossed blob's target is between the jumper's origin and... no. Let me try: the crossed blob's target is occupied by the jumper's origin? T5: crossed blob1, target 29; jumper's origin 23. No. T10: crossed blob2, target 11; jumper's origin 17. No.
What if: catastrophe when the jumper's target is the crossed blob's... T5: jumper's target 11, crossed blob1's target 29. T10: jumper's target 29, crossed blob2's target 11. Interesting!! T5: jumper's target (11) = the other blob's (blob2's) target... no wait, blob2 is the jumper. T5: jumper=blob2 (target 11), crossed=blob1 (target 29). T10: jumper=blob1 (target 29), crossed=blob2 (target 11). In both cases, the jumper's target and the crossed blob's target are 11 and 29. Symmetric! Argh.
OK, let me give up on the explanation and just accept the uncertainty. The planned jump 35→23 (leftward, crossing 29) is most similar to T5 (leftward crossing) → probably a catastrophe. A catastrophe gives: blob1+blob3 erased, verticals gray, key appears.
Is that state useful? If the goal is "all blobs settled/gray or cleared" → maybe a win. If the goal is "all on targets" → dead end (undo).
Given I'm stuck on the goal, the catastrophe is the most informative remaining move: it tests whether the post-catastrophe state (no horizontal blobs, gray verticals) completes the level. If it doesn't complete, I undo with the key and have lost nothing but time (timer: ~44 steps left).
Alternative: maybe I should reconsider that the vertical blobs are selectable — perhaps they require a double-click or a click on a specific pixel. T14 (37,42) and T16 (25,43) did nothing. Let me try one more: (26,42) and (38,42) — the exact centers. If still nothing, they're obstacles.
Actually, let me reconsider the whole thing once more. What if the vertical blobs are the "player" and the horizontal blobs are obstacles? No — the horizontal blobs are selectable.
What if the goal is to move all blobs to the vertical arm (the "goal zone")? The L-shape: horizontal arm = start, vertical arm = goal? The vertical blobs at 24,36 are already in the goal zone. The horizontal blobs need to reach the vertical arm... but they can only jump within the horizontal arm (targets 11/23/29). Hmm, no.
What if the goal is: fill the vertical arm's slots (24,28,32,36,40) with blobs? Currently 24,36 are filled. Need 28,32,40. The horizontal blobs' targets are horizontal. No.
Let me just go with the catastrophe probe. No wait — actually, let me reconsider one more time.
Hmm, what if the T5 catastrophe was a coincidence of the timer? No, the timer is row 0 only.
What if the catastrophe is: a jump crossing a blob erases the crossed blob, and additionally, if the crossed blob was the last...? At T5, after erasing blob1, the horizontal blobs = only blob2 (the jumper). At T10, after erasing blob2, the horizontal blobs = blob1 (the jumper) + blob3. So T5: the crossing leaves only 1 horizontal blob; T10: leaves 2. Catastrophe when "only 1 horizontal blob remains"?? That's a weird rule. But it fits! And the verticals turning gray = "settled because the game is nearly over"?
If that's the rule, then the planned 35→23 jump (crossing 29): after erasing blob1, horizontal = only blob3 → catastrophe again. Same result.
Either way, the 35→23 jump → probably a catastrophe. Let me execute it and see if the level completes.
Plan:
1. MOUSE(19,36) — select blob3 (center pixel (19,36) is part of blob3: yes, (19,36) is a pixel).
2. MOUSE(19,24) — click the target ring at slot (18,23): the ring's hollow center ≈ (19,24)/(20,24). The ring pixels are (19,23),(19,26),(20,23),(20,26),(18,24),(18,25),(21,24),(21,25). Consistent.

Let me execute steps 1-2 as a batch, then inspect.
